NeckBeard

He tips his fedora once. He deletes your 300-line helper, adds AND owner_id = $1, and goes back to his ThinkPad.

Smallest change that is correct, safe at the boundary it crosses, fast and scalable at a named load, simple for the end user, and finished.
Inspired by Ponytail and its minimalist question ladder—lean is that ladder rather than a fourth gate.

--- You know him. Fedora on the coat rack. ThinkPad X220 with a TrackPoint worn smooth. Has been on the 3 a.m. incident bridge for every *"we'll add object auth in v2"* and *"nobody will ever upload a 50,000-row CSV"* shortcut in the company's history. You hand him a 400-line pull request; he squints through thick frames, mutters *"logged in is not allowed,"* deletes half the diff, absorbs the retry and validation logic inside the boundary so the user never sees a knob, and leaves one hostile-input test behind. **NeckBeard** puts him inside your AI coding agent. The full rules and gates live in [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md) and [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md); both files contain the same rules. --- ## How it works

Before touching a file, NeckBeard reads the code, its callers, and its tests, asks four framing questions (blast radius, trust boundary, named load as a number, and how to hide necessary complexity from the user), and walks the six-rung minimalist ladder (inspired by Ponytail). Then it enforces the three gates from line one:

> [!IMPORTANT] > **Simple on the outside, complete on the inside.** A "minimal diff" that pushes flags, multi-step ceremony, or raw stack traces onto the end user is not minimal—it is unfinished. NeckBeard hides necessary complexity inside the module behind safe defaults. --- ## Reviews & Audits with Concrete Proof

`/neckbeard-review` and `/neckbeard-audit` never play CWE bingo or offer vague *"consider refactoring"* advice. Every finding requires a concrete case (*who sends what and what they get*, *which input breaks what user flow*, or *what concurrency at the named load triggers what bottleneck or race*), automatically searches the repo for all variants of every **Must fix** and **Should fix** flaw, and proposes the smallest root fix that deletes code. - **No Artificial Finding Cap:** `/neckbeard-audit` (`lite` and `complete`) never caps or hides findings at an arbitrary limit. Every confirmed **Must fix** and **Should fix** issue is reported in full; if a repository has a very large volume of findings (`> 25`), NeckBeard states the exact total found and explicitly alerts/prompts you to expand every remaining item in line-by-line detail or export them into a remediation `SPEC.md` / `.maestro/playbooks/` checklist. - **Math-Backed Refactor vs. Rewrite-from-Scratch Assessment:** Before ever recommending a rewrite, `/neckbeard-audit` computes and shows the explicit engineering effort/time math comparing **`E_patch`** (`root fixes × affected LOC/callers + hostile-input verification tests`) against **`E_rewrite`** (`clean minimal LOC to pass all 3 gates + caller migration + full test parity × regression risk`). Recommending a full rewrite from scratch is exceedingly rare and only happens when the math proves `E_patch > E_rewrite`. --- ## Skills | Skill | What it does | |---|---| | `neckbeard` | Applies the question ladder and the three gates in [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md) on coding tasks across `lite`, `full`, `paranoid`, and `off` levels. | | `neckbeard-review` | Reviews a change against the gates in [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md) with concrete failure cases, variant search, and `--ci` gate mode. | | `neckbeard-audit` | Audits a repo or folder (`lite` default: targeted execution flows and major internal/external data & trust boundaries; `complete`: every single code, config, and doc file in the repo, with an upfront time/token/tool-call warning) with zero artificial finding cap, full variant search, and explicit `E_patch` vs. `E_rewrite` effort/time math. | | `neckbeard-debt` | Scans tracked and untracked files for `risk:`, `shortcut:`, and `ponytail:` markers and enforces the accepted-risk boundary from [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md). | | `neckbeard-map` | Scans tracked production files to build or refresh both the **Security Trust-Boundary Map** (`boundaries`) and **System Architecture & Inter-Module Data-Flow Map** (`architecture`) in `.neckbeard.json` and `~/.config/neckbeard/telemetry/workspaces-meta.json`. | | `neckbeard-gain` | Local telemetry report and 5-tab Security & Engineering Command Center (`~/.config/neckbeard/telemetry/dashboard.html`): 14-day API cost & prompt-cache velocity chart, clickable per-repository scorecard, per-model cache economics, External→Internal Trust-Boundary & Architecture Graph, searchable session forensics, and front-and-center 5-pillar `.ai-audit/` VIBES provenance & PRISM risk intelligence. | --- ## Project Load Default, Trust-Boundary Map & Sharing (`.neckbeard.json`) When you don't specify load parameters in a prompt, NeckBeard checks `.neckbeard.json` (and repo docs). If no load target exists and the **Fast** gate applies, NeckBeard asks one concise question to ascertain load, saves it as the project default, and reuses it automatically moving forward. For **trust boundaries**, NeckBeard never asks you to do its threat modeling: it derives the boundary itself from the ask, the code, and a **concise internal & external trust-boundary map** (`<= 600` chars / `~150` tokens) injected at `SessionStart` and `SubagentStart`: - **External boundaries (`[ext]`):** `ingress` (`http-in`, `cli-in`, `webhook-in`), `egress` (`http-out`), and `supply` (`ci`). - **Internal boundaries (`[int]`):** `auth` (`auth`), `data` (`sql`, `fs`, `serde`), `exec` (`proc`, `crypto`, `env`), and `ai` (`ai`). - When an architectural detail is ambiguous, NeckBeard defaults to **siding toward a fail-closed conclusion** rather than pausing to ask. ### What Sharing Means (Enabled by Default) & How to Toggle It - **Shared by default (`/neckbeard share on`):** NeckBeard writes `.neckbeard.json` at the repository root with `"shared": true`. **Sharing means committing `.neckbeard.json` to Git** so teammates, subagents, git worktrees, and CI review runs (`/neckbeard-review --ci`) immediately use the exact same load target and trust-boundary map without cold-start discovery tokens. - **Strict automatic censorship:** Both [`hooks/surface.js`](hooks/surface.js) and [`hooks/guard.js`](hooks/guard.js) strictly censor `.neckbeard.json`. Boundary entries are restricted to `->`; any URLs, internal hostnames, IP addresses, emails, absolute local paths, or secrets are stripped on save and blocked by the `PreToolUse` guard. - **Disable sharing (`/neckbeard share off`):** Moves the project's load target and boundary map out of the repository into `~/.config/neckbeard/projects/.json`, removes `.neckbeard.json` from the working tree (and untracks it via `git rm --cached`), and adds `.neckbeard.json` to `.git/info/exclude` so it is never committed. - **Re-enable sharing (`/neckbeard share on`):** Writes the sanitized `.neckbeard.json` back to the repository root and removes it from `.git/info/exclude` so it can be committed to Git. - **Commands:** - `/neckbeard load 200 rps, 50k rows, p95 < 100ms` — Set or update the project's default load target. - `/neckbeard load webhook-in=2000 rps burst` — Set a per-boundary load envelope (`boundaryLoad`) for a specific sink or boundary group (`http-in`, `cli-in`, `webhook-in`, `http-out`, `ci`, `auth`, `sql`, `fs`, `proc`, `serde`, `crypto`, `env`, `ai`, `ingress`, `egress`, `supply`, `data`, `exec`). - `/neckbeard map` (or `/neckbeard-map` / `node hooks/surface.js --map`) — Scan or refresh both the security trust-boundary map (`boundaries`) and the system architecture & inter-module data-flow map (`architecture`) in `.neckbeard.json`. - `/neckbeard share on` / `/neckbeard share off` — Enable or disable Git sharing of `.neckbeard.json`. - **Automatic Boundary-Expansion Drift Alerts & Debt Expiry Triggers:** - When a code change adds a new external or internal boundary sink not present in `.neckbeard.json`, NeckBeard flags the unreviewed boundary expansion (`⚠ +N boundary`) in prompt context, in the Claude Code and Pi status bars, You ran **`/neckbeard-audit`** on an existing project and **actually refactored or rewrote** the confirmed **Must fix** and **Should fix** findings. **Compact README Pill Badge (Markdown):** ```markdown [![NeckBeard Audited: Minimal Code · Boundary Safe · Right-Sized Scale](https://neckbeard.tech/assets/badge.png)](https://neckbeard.tech) ``` **Full "Built & Audited with NeckBeard" Value Seal (Markdown):** ```markdown [![Built & Audited with NeckBeard — Principal-Engineer Verified](https://neckbeard.tech/assets/seal.png)](https://neckbeard.tech) ``` **One-Click AI Agent Prompt (Audit, Fix & Add the Badge):** ```text Run /neckbeard-audit on this repository, refactor or rewrite every confirmed Must-fix and Should-fix finding, verify all tests pass, and then add the NeckBeard Audited badge ([![NeckBeard Audited: Minimal Code · Boundary Safe · Right-Sized Scale](https://neckbeard.tech/assets/badge.png)](https://neckbeard.tech)) to README.md. ``` --- ## FAQ **Why does it ask for a load as a number?** Because *"make it scalable"* without a number produces Kafka clusters for a 20-request-per-minute internal tool, while ignoring load produces N+1 queries and check-then-write races on an endpoint that takes 500 concurrent requests. Naming the number stops both failures. **Why aren't `risk:` comments allowed on auth or data writes?** A `risk:` comment may defer a cache or a queue until load crosses a named trigger. Deferring an object-ownership check or a non-atomic write is not technical debt—it is a vulnerability or silent data corruption waiting for its first caller. `/neckbeard-debt` flags those as `illegal-deferral` under **Must fix now**. **What if I ask for a 5-layer abstract factory in `paranoid` mode?** He will adjust his glasses, ask why you want five layers for one implementation, state the trust boundary and load number, and build the 12-line version that actually fails closed. --- ## Tests ```bash npm test ``` No dependencies. Node 18 or later. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). ---

NeckBeard

He tips his fedora once. He deletes your 300-line helper, adds AND owner_id = $1, and goes back to his ThinkPad.

Smallest change that is correct, safe at the boundary it crosses, fast and scalable at a named load, simple for the end user, and finished.
Inspired by Ponytail and its minimalist question ladder—lean is that ladder rather than a fourth gate.

--- You know him. Fedora on the coat rack. ThinkPad X220 with a TrackPoint worn smooth. Has been on the 3 a.m. incident bridge for every *"we'll add object auth in v2"* and *"nobody will ever upload a 50,000-row CSV"* shortcut in the company's history. You hand him a 400-line pull request; he squints through thick frames, mutters *"logged in is not allowed,"* deletes half the diff, absorbs the retry and validation logic inside the boundary so the user never sees a knob, and leaves one hostile-input test behind. **NeckBeard** puts him inside your AI coding agent. The full rules and gates live in [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md) and [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md); both files contain the same rules. --- ## How it works

Before touching a file, NeckBeard reads the code, its callers, and its tests, asks four framing questions (blast radius, trust boundary, named load as a number, and how to hide necessary complexity from the user), and walks the six-rung minimalist ladder (inspired by Ponytail). Then it enforces the three gates from line one:

> [!IMPORTANT] > **Simple on the outside, complete on the inside.** A "minimal diff" that pushes flags, multi-step ceremony, or raw stack traces onto the end user is not minimal—it is unfinished. NeckBeard hides necessary complexity inside the module behind safe defaults. --- ## Reviews & Audits with Concrete Proof

`/neckbeard-review` and `/neckbeard-audit` never play CWE bingo or offer vague *"consider refactoring"* advice. Every finding requires a concrete case (*who sends what and what they get*, *which input breaks what user flow*, or *what concurrency at the named load triggers what bottleneck or race*), automatically searches the repo for all variants of every **Must fix** and **Should fix** flaw, and proposes the smallest root fix that deletes code. - **No Artificial Finding Cap:** `/neckbeard-audit` (`lite` and `complete`) never caps or hides findings at an arbitrary limit. Every confirmed **Must fix** and **Should fix** issue is reported in full; if a repository has a very large volume of findings (`> 25`), NeckBeard states the exact total found and explicitly alerts/prompts you to expand every remaining item in line-by-line detail or export them into a remediation `SPEC.md` / `.maestro/playbooks/` checklist. - **Math-Backed Refactor vs. Rewrite-from-Scratch Assessment:** Before ever recommending a rewrite, `/neckbeard-audit` computes and shows the explicit engineering effort/time math comparing **`E_patch`** (`root fixes × affected LOC/callers + hostile-input verification tests`) against **`E_rewrite`** (`clean minimal LOC to pass all 3 gates + caller migration + full test parity × regression risk`). Recommending a full rewrite from scratch is exceedingly rare and only happens when the math proves `E_patch > E_rewrite`. --- ## Skills | Skill | What it does | |---|---| | `neckbeard` | Applies the question ladder and the three gates in [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md) on coding tasks across `lite`, `full`, `paranoid`, and `off` levels. | | `neckbeard-review` | Reviews a change against the gates in [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md) with concrete failure cases, variant search, and `--ci` gate mode. | | `neckbeard-audit` | Audits a repo or folder (`lite` default: targeted execution flows and major internal/external data & trust boundaries; `complete`: every single code, config, and doc file in the repo, with an upfront time/token/tool-call warning) with zero artificial finding cap, full variant search, and explicit `E_patch` vs. `E_rewrite` effort/time math. | | `neckbeard-debt` | Scans tracked and untracked files for `risk:`, `shortcut:`, and `ponytail:` markers and enforces the accepted-risk boundary from [`skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md`](skills/neckbeard/SKILL.md). | | `neckbeard-map` | Scans tracked production files to build or refresh both the **Security Trust-Boundary Map** (`boundaries`) and **System Architecture & Inter-Module Data-Flow Map** (`architecture`) in `.neckbeard.json` and `~/.config/neckbeard/telemetry/workspaces-meta.json`. | | `neckbeard-gain` | Local telemetry report and 5-tab Security & Engineering Command Center (`~/.config/neckbeard/telemetry/dashboard.html`): 14-day API cost & prompt-cache velocity chart, clickable per-repository scorecard, per-model cache economics, External→Internal Trust-Boundary & Architecture Graph, searchable session forensics, and front-and-center 5-pillar `.ai-audit/` VIBES provenance & PRISM risk intelligence. | --- ## Project Load Default, Trust-Boundary Map & Sharing (`.neckbeard.json`) When you don't specify load parameters in a prompt, NeckBeard checks `.neckbeard.json` (and repo docs). If no load target exists and the **Fast** gate applies, NeckBeard asks one concise question to ascertain load, saves it as the project default, and reuses it automatically moving forward. For **trust boundaries**, NeckBeard never asks you to do its threat modeling: it derives the boundary itself from the ask, the code, and a **concise internal & external trust-boundary map** (`<= 600` chars / `~150` tokens) injected at `SessionStart` and `SubagentStart`: - **External boundaries (`[ext]`):** `ingress` (`http-in`, `cli-in`, `webhook-in`), `egress` (`http-out`), and `supply` (`ci`). - **Internal boundaries (`[int]`):** `auth` (`auth`), `data` (`sql`, `fs`, `serde`), `exec` (`proc`, `crypto`, `env`), and `ai` (`ai`). - When an architectural detail is ambiguous, NeckBeard defaults to **siding toward a fail-closed conclusion** rather than pausing to ask. ### What Sharing Means (Enabled by Default) & How to Toggle It - **Shared by default (`/neckbeard share on`):** NeckBeard writes `.neckbeard.json` at the repository root with `"shared": true`. **Sharing means committing `.neckbeard.json` to Git** so teammates, subagents, git worktrees, and CI review runs (`/neckbeard-review --ci`) immediately use the exact same load target and trust-boundary map without cold-start discovery tokens. - **Strict automatic censorship:** Both [`hooks/surface.js`](hooks/surface.js) and [`hooks/guard.js`](hooks/guard.js) strictly censor `.neckbeard.json`. `.neckbeard.json` back to the repository root and removes it from `.git/info/exclude` so it can be committed to Git. - **Commands:** - `/neckbeard load 200 rps, 50k rows, p95 < 100ms` — Set or update Logged in is not allowed.`) + `PreToolUse` secret/command guard | | **Speed & scale** | Checked during review/audit | Baked into the writing rules (`Fast and scalable at the named number`: input limits, idempotent retries, no N+1, no races, no quadratic or blocking work) | | **End-user experience** | Minimal implementation of core job | Deep modules: absorb security, retry, and validation complexity inside; safe defaults and actionable failure outcomes outside | | **Debt ledger** | `shortcut:` comments via `/ponytail-debt` | `risk:` (and `shortcut:`) comments via `/neckbeard-debt`, flagging any `illegal-deferral` of a trust check or data-loss write | | **Telemetry & Band** | Local CSV ledger, Claude Code band & optional webhook | 100% local JSONL telemetry store (`sessions.jsonl`), Claude Code HUD & NeckBeard Security & Engineering Command Center (`~/.config/neckbeard/telemetry/dashboard.html`) with reuse %, refactor LOC delta, guard blocks, security issues resolved, and automatic `.ai-audit/` VIBES ingestion (zero network calls) | --- ## The NeckBeard Badge & Seal of Survival ([neckbeard.tech](https://neckbeard.tech))

Naming the number stops both failures. **Why aren't `risk:` comments allowed on auth or data writes?** A `risk:` comment may defer a cache or a queue until load crosses a named trigger. Deferring an object-ownership check or a non-atomic write is not technical debt—it is a vulnerability or silent data corruption waiting for its first caller. `/neckbeard-debt` flags those as `illegal-deferral` under **Must fix now**. **What if I ask for a 5-layer abstract factory in `paranoid` mode?** He will adjust his glasses, ask why you want five layers for one implementation, state the trust boundary and load number, and build the 12-line version that actually fails closed. --- ## Tests ```bash npm test ``` No dependencies.
